literal: Even when having attained completeness there, there is indeed no benefit for a country that lacks harmony with its ruler.
translation: Even if a country has acquired all other forms of excellence, it is of no use if it lacks a ruler who governs in harmony with his people.
modern: அனைத்துச் சிறப்புகளையும் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், நல்லாட்சி செய்யும் அரசன் இல்லாத நாடு எந்தப் பயனையும் தராது.
explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on the country by emphasizing that physical and economic resources are meaningless without proper governance. The phrase 'vēntu amaivu' refers to the fitness of the ruler and the harmony between the ruler and the subjects. Even if a land possesses natural wealth, security, and prosperity, these assets yield no real benefit if there is no capable leader to manage and protect them. Thus, a good ruler is the ultimate requirement that gives value to all other virtues of a nation.
